title: Onprem install cadence sync — July 2026
content:
Weekly sync notes + standup capture — compact view (working doc)

Meeting context:
- Purpose: consolidate outstanding install/customer blockers for VPC/on-prem installs, align owners for next 72h, and surface risks to SRE and Solutions Eng.
- Attendees: Aisha (owner), Diego (network), Priya (installer), Lena (security), Marco (field eng), + Solutions Eng: Tom
- Tone: working notes, not polished. Keep actionable items with owners and dates.

Key updates since last week:
1) Zenith customer (onprem) — rack-level L2 mismatch
   - Symptom: install failed during fabric bring-up; switch ports flapping after PXE stage.
   - Root cause (investigating): vendor-provided TOR had incorrect LLDP config and a mix of MLAG vs single-switch assumptions. CLI showed unauthenticated LLDP neighbor changes.
   - Impact: install delayed by ~48h, staging cluster booting ok but cannot join fabric for KV-cache warmup.
   - Current action: Diego to validate TOR LLDP settings (commands saved in linked_artifacts MR). Priya scheduled remote session with customer network admin Friday 7/16.
   - Blocker severity: high (blocks go-live).

2) VPC install for HyperEdge trial — IAM/service account propagation
   - Symptom: kube nodes created but init containers crash on secret pull (403).
   - Hypothesis: role binding applied to wrong namespace during bootstrap script v0.9.1.
   - Action: Marco rolled temporary workaround to use cluster-admin role for installer service-account; Lena to file minimal-privilege follow-up and map required perms. Patch scheduled for 7/14.
   - Blocker severity: medium. Workaround in place but security review required before GA.

3) Telemetry ingestion gap (onprem)
   - Problem: install telemetry from two onprem installs shows 30–40% of orchestrator events dropped during initial KV warmup window.
   - Investigation notes: transient S3 retries and some TLS renegotiation on customer-side proxy.
   - Next: Priya to add additional verbose logs for the collector and increase client-side backoff. Diego to ask customer to allow larger keepalive on proxy.

Standup-style quick blockers / asks (each line = owner — short ask):
- Aisha — need ETA from Zenith network team (target: 7/16 11:00 PT).
- Diego — will push LLDP checklist to repo (PR 431) by EOD 7/13. Reviewers: Marco + Priya.
- Priya — needs remote console access token from HyperEdge (still pending). Ticket PS-4821.
- Lena — requires copy of customer's internal KMS policy before approving reduced-privilege patch.
- Marco — requests telemetry traces from last 3 failed installs (prefiltered). Diego will upload to shared bucket by 7/13.

Action items (owner — action — due):
- Diego — run TOR LLDP validation script (tools/network/tor-validate.sh) against Zenith lab and share results — due 2026-07-13.
- Priya — remote install session with Zenith (coordinate with customer net admin) and attempt fabric rejoin — due 2026-07-16.
- Marco — cut hotfix for RBAC mapping in bootstrap script and deploy to staging (branch: rbac-hotfix/2026-07) — due 2026-07-14.
- Lena — produce minimal-privilege permission matrix (doc) for installer service-account — due 2026-07-17.
- Aisha — escalate go/no-go threshold to EPD manager if Zenith not recovered by 7/17.
- Priya + Diego — instrument collector verbose logs and retry windows; push as opt-in flag for field installs — due 2026-07-15.

Open questions / unknowns (notes-to-self):
- Is LLDP across vendor TORs a reproducible failure mode in our staging? We have 1/6 fabric types covered in lab. Need test matrix.
- Should we change default bootstrap to tolerate partial fabric for first-pass KV warmup? Pros: faster installs; Cons: added complexity and potential inconsistent cache state.
- What is acceptable telemetry loss percentage during bootstrap for SRE? Current SLO undefined for first 30 minutes. Flag for SRE to define.

Logs & quick diagnostic snippets (copied for field eng):
- Example TOR dump showing LLDP state: sudo net show lldp brief | grep -i error  # (captured 2026-07-12 09:12)
- Installer backtrace: /var/log/redwood/installer.log tail -n 200 | grep -E "error|panic|traceback"
- Collector verbose command toggle: REDWOOD_COLLECTOR_VERBOSE=true ./collector --mode=field --retry-window=15s

Risk assessment (short):
- Zenith remaining risk: high until fabric stable. If unresolved >72h, we must offer expanded field-support or swap TOR hardware (cost).
- HyperEdge trial: low-medium risk, controlled with RBAC hotfix. Main risk is delayed security sign-off.
- Telemetry: operational inconvenience; must define tolerances to avoid false OLA escalations.

Customer communications (draft snippets for Solutions Eng):
- To Zenith network admin (email draft): "We saw LLDP neighbor churn during fabric bring-up; before the remote session please capture the output of 'show lldp neighbors detail' and ensure MLAG config matches our runbook. We'll attempt a controlled rejoin on 7/16 and can pause if you prefer manual oversight."
- To HyperEdge PM: "We applied a temporary RBAC workaround so the install can continue; we'll schedule the secure patch for 7/14 and will not leave cluster with elevated permissions in production."

Notes / follow-ups to add to runbook (actionable doc changes):
- Add LLDP preflight checklist (commands + expected outputs) and vendor-specific gotchas.
- Expand installer bootstrap logging level in field mode and include explicit retry/backoff knobs.
- Add a short section on acceptable telemetry loss during first 30m and how to escalate to SRE.

Meeting retrospective (quick):
- What went well: fast owner assignment, temporary workarounds kept installs moving for non-critical paths.
- What to improve: preflight network checks need to be part of every customer onboarding checklist; signal gaps in telemetry should be flagged to SRE with a short SLA.

Next sync cadence:
- Daily 15m standup until Zenith fabric rejoins (time: 09:30 PT). Weekly long-sync Friday 10:30 PT for broader installs status.

End of working note — will convert to polished incident summary if Zenith remains high-severity after 72h.

Unresolved (personal TODOs):
- Build minimal test harness in lab to emulate vendor LLDP misconfig (ticket: OPS-212).
- Draft short internal playbook for RBAC bootstrap rollback steps.
